A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Match-and-Fuse. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-C can be reliably matched; v2 additionally contains Appendix D. No material reading gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, quantitative comparisons, ablations, runtime measurements, and a user study with 1,600 judgments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a qualitative downstream video-advertisement experiment in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The Pairwise Consistency Graph, Multiview Feature Fusion, Feature Guidance, and FlowEdit integration remain unchanged. Appendix D uses edited images as inputs to an external video generator without revising the proposed Match-and-Fuse procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds a multi-cut video-advertisement scenario requiring product consistency across generated video cuts. The original 149-set, 400-edit benchmark and its dataset composition remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The existing comparisons retain FLUX, FLUX Kontext, IC-LoRA, and Edicho; Section 4.3 merely reorders their descriptions. Figure D.8 reuses FLUX.1-dev and FLUX Kontext. Wan is the downstream video generator, not an added comparator.

E3.justification: The new demonstration introduces keyframe-conditioned video generation across three cuts: Wan2.1-FLF2V for the first and Wan2.1-I2V for the other two. Existing benchmark metrics, image-generation settings, and user-study procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure D.8 adds a comparative case study testing whether consistent edited keyframes support coherent multi-cut advertisements. Existing component ablations, match-sparsity and set-size tests, runtime analyses, and extended-attention experiments are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 6 retains SEM error bars, Table 1 retains its uncertainty reporting, and Appendix A.2 retains the same seed information. The added qualitative example introduces no repeated-run information or statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Figure D.8 adds generated video-frame examples and reports better cross-cut product consistency than FLUX.1-dev and FLUX Kontext. Existing numerical results are unchanged, including Match-and-Fuse's Table 1 DINO-MatchSim score of 0.80 ± 0.003.

T1.justification: The method, metric, and appendix equations are retained. Section 3.3 aligns coordinate membership notation with the already-defined mapping M_ij: C_i -> C_j; this does not change the mathematical construction or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims about training-free, mask-free unstructured set-to-set generation, superior consistency, and the DINO-MatchSim metric. The added application supports the existing creative-use motivation.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds the interpretation that consistent keyframe editing enables coherent multi-cut advertisements where independent image editing fails. Existing limitations concerning correspondences, disocclusions, conditioning fidelity, and FlowEdit tuning remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Figure D.8 identifies the Wan2.1 variants used downstream. The abstract replaces future-release wording with 'Code and data: project page,' retaining the same link; actual release availability is not established by the PDFs. Existing implementation settings are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Wan video-generation reference, cited by Figure D.8. Existing related-work discussions and research positioning remain unchanged; subsequent reference-number changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited abstract and method wording edits, reorders baseline descriptions, and adds a short Appendix D. The main organization is retained. The new appendix incorrectly refers to Section 3.3 for extended applications, which appear in Section 4.5.

P2.justification: v2 makes local graphical revisions to the pipeline/MFF illustrations in Figures 3-4 and adds the multi-cut comparison in Figure D.8. Existing result figures and table structures are retained, with minor text reflow.

improvement.justification: Appendix D turns v1's product-advertisement motivation into a concrete downstream demonstration, modestly strengthening evidence of practical usefulness. The gain is limited: quantitative validation is unchanged, and the single qualitative example does not establish the caption's sweeping claim of 'infinite coherent edits.'
